# Measure memory and page-cache pressure for N=8 session snapshots

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 4.

## Target outcome

The resource cost of holding 8 session snapshots instead of 2: per-snapshot
footprint, bytes per token, aggregate on-disk and host page-cache growth at N=8,
and the system `MemAvailable` delta — with VRAM reported as non-available rather
than guessed, per the fidelity convention in
`docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`.

## Minimal implementation

- `--mode memory` in the harness: build N=8 distinct session prefixes, save all
  eight (bounded by free page cache), then measure:
  - on-disk size per snapshot and total (also reported by
    `du -sb` on the run's own directory);
  - `/proc/meminfo` `Cached` and `MemAvailable` before/after each save and after
    the full set, plus the page-cache residency of the snapshot files;
  - read-back bandwidth: sequential read of each snapshot to `/dev/null` (the
    proxy's restore path reads the whole file), giving MiB/s — the term that
    determines restore cost as snapshots grow.
- Derive bytes/token per size and extrapolate to N=8 for a realistic mix,
  stating the mix used.
- Record the ROCm VRAM reading and mark it explicitly non-available/ungraded
  (the known-degraded ~0.2 GB reading), instead of reporting a false number.
- Emit `results/<label>/memory.json` + markdown table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-size snapshot footprint and bytes/token, measured (not derived-only).
- N=8 aggregate footprint (sum of snapshot sizes) and observed `Cached` growth,
  with the delta between them explained (page cache vs. written-but-not-resident).
- `MemAvailable` delta across a full N=8 set, and the maximum resident footprint
  observed during the run.
- Read-back bandwidth (MiB/s) for snapshot files, which the verdict uses to
  extrapolate restore cost.
- VRAM is either measured credibly or explicitly reported as non-available with
  the reason; no estimated VRAM figure is presented as measured.
- The run cleans up the snapshots it created and reports the post-cleanup
  `MemAvailable` / `Cached` return-to-baseline.

## Constraints

- Must not fill the page cache to the point of harming live inference: the run
  is bounded by a `--max-write-mib` guard (default sized from current
  `MemAvailable`) and stops early, recording truncation.
- No `drop_caches` unless explicitly permitted by the operator; measure the
  natural page-cache behaviour instead.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/kv_memory_table.py` (per-token KV expectation reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/memory.json` (new artifact)
- `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`

# Results doc: tables, break-even model, go/no-go verdict and substitutes

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Satisfies AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC5 of the spike.

## Target outcome

A committed document `docs/virtual-slot-spike-LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE.md` containing
the complete measured tables, an explicit break-even inequality, a go/no-go
verdict, and — if not viable — the cheaper substitutes ranked with the measured
evidence for each.

## Minimal implementation

- Assemble the tables from the four measurement children's JSON artifacts
  (save size/time, restore time, restore hit-rate, invalidated-restore rate,
  memory delta, contention A/B). Cross-link each number to its result file and
  commit so the doc is auditable, not just descriptive.
- Break-even model, stated as an inequality with every term measured:
  `hit_rate × (cold_prefill_s − restore_s) > (1 − hit_rate) × eviction_reprefill_s + save_s_share`
  — or an equivalent explicit form — with the measured values substituted and
  the resulting break-even `hit_rate*` solved for each prompt size. State the
  cold-prefill baseline used (window median 61.8 s dispatch-first-byte, p90
  269.8 s) and the solitary cold-prefill figures from the parent's impact
  analysis (~254 new tok/s).
- Verdict: `go` (build virtual slots) / `no-go` (not viable) / `conditional`
  (viable only under a named condition), each with the driving measurement
  quoted. If `no-go`, rank the substitutes with measured evidence:
  more physical slots (LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8 — keep N=2 pending
  LP-0MVGPEP3O000RKKD), idle-aware admission (LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J implementation
  done; LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD / LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF measurement), shorter
  post-stream lease (locate and cite the owning item).
- Fidelity section reproducing the caveat conventions
  (`docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`): what could not be measured,
  VRAM non-availability, and the live-load validity caveat if applicable.
- AC5 proof: a `No production behaviour change` section listing the commits
  touched (`git diff --stat` restricted to `proxy/benchmarks/`, `proxy/tests/`,
  `docs/`), confirming `proxy/config.yaml` sha unchanged and proxy healthy after
  the runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/virtual-slot-spike-LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE.md` committed with all six
  required tables: save size/time, restore time, restore hit-rate,
  invalidated-restore rate, memory delta, end-to-end contention metrics.
- The break-even condition is an explicit inequality with measured terms
  substituted, and the break-even hit-rate is solved per prompt size.
- Verdict is one of `go` / `no-go` / `conditional`, with the decisive measurement
  quoted and linked to its result artifact.
- If `no-go` or `conditional`, at least three cheaper substitutes are named with
  the measured evidence for each (or, where a substitute is unmeasured, that is
  stated as an open measurement with the owning work-item id).
- A fidelity/caveats section states every non-measured quantity explicitly, with
  no estimated value presented as measured.
- AC5 is evidenced: the diff touches only benchmark/test/doc paths, config sha
  unchanged, proxy verified healthy after the runs.
- Every number in the doc traces to a committed result file.

## Constraints

- Read-only on production configuration. No items in `proxy/proxy/` modified.
- The doc must not re-derive historical baselines it can cite (61.8 s median,
  269.8 s p90 from the parent's window).

## Key Files

- `docs/virtual-slot-spike-LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE.md` (new)
- `docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md` (format/caveat reference)
- `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` (validity-caveat reference)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the parent item's gating precondition verified from
measured evidence, so that prefill tuning only starts once local actually
carries sustained work.

## What the gate is

Parent **LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT** AC0 requires a comment recording a measured
**>60 % local (GPU) busy** night before any change is made. Busy is the
`## Local model utilization` upper bound (dispatch -> finish: prefill +
decode) from the deterministic `proxy-usage-analysis` CLI, over a complete
night window (22:00-07:00 local).

## Evidence at planning time (2026-10-25)

- Night **2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00**: busy **2.2 %** (719 s of
  32 400 s; 27 local streams; prefill 336 slot-s; decode 383 slot-s;
  idle 97.8 %).
  Command:
  `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "2026-10-23 22:00:00" --end "2026-10-24 07:00:00" --output-dir /tmp/wl-gate-check --json`
- Same night in the 24 h daily report (`~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`,
  window 2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52): busy 10.2 %.

**The gate is NOT met.** The parent is left `blocked` at stage
`plan_complete`, and every other child of this plan depends on this item, so
none of them is dispatchable until the gate passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0: The gate AC is satisfied - a comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation for a full night, from the usage-analysis report, before any change is made.
- AC1: A comment on the parent records local busy % for a **complete** night
  window (22:00-07:00), with the exact CLI invocation, the window bounds and
  the artifact directory used.
- AC2: The gate is declared met **only** when `busy_pct >= 60` for the whole
  night (`definition: dispatch_to_finish` in the CLI `--json` summary).
- AC3: When the gate is not met this item stays **open and incomplete** with
  the evidence comment (recorded `blocked` status is derived from dependency
  edges in `wl` and cannot be pinned, so this item is the lock: keeping it
  incomplete keeps every dependent child dependency-blocked), and no other
  child of the plan is started.
- AC6: This item must never be marked `completed` while the gate is unmet. If a
  run cannot leave it open, it records the evidence and files the deferral on
  the parent rather than completing the gate.
- AC4: When the gate is met this item completes with the evidence comment and
  the parent plus its dependent siblings are unblocked in the same update
  sequence.
- AC5: Measurement only - no configuration, flag or code change.

**Key Files:**
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` - deterministic report CLI
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` - report section definitions

## Dependencies

None. All other children of this plan depend on this item.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want Arm A (the current 2 x 131,072 geometry) captured over a
gate-compliant night window, so there is a like-for-like baseline for Arm B.

- Current geometry: `--parallel 2`, `--ctx-size 262144` => per-slot 131,072; `session_slot_pool_size: 2`; warm ceiling ~120,049 (= 0.4578 x 262,144) below the 126,976 per-slot clamp; cold threshold 38,000.

## Goal

Compute the verdict, propagate the result, update documentation and pass the
test gate, per parent AC6/AC8/AC9/AC10 of `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K`. This is the
final child of the measurement.

## Scheduling — earliest implementation time

**Runnable only after both C2 (baseline replay) and C3 (measurement +
classification) have produced their results** (at/after `2026-10-28T10:17:00Z`
plus their run time). On FAIL it must create a `discovered-from` item, so it may
spawn follow-up work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC6 — Verdict recorded with both gates.** **PASS** requires (i) 90 %
  reduction and (ii) no refusal window over 180 s.
- **AC8 — Result recorded and propagated.** One structured result comment on
  this item with the verdict, cross-referenced from the epic and the sibling
  item.
- **AC9 — Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/slot-thrashing-investigation/findings.md`
  gains the measured window, verdict and corrected invocation.
- **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (executed
  via the test skill).
- **C4.1 — Both gates applied.** PASS iff (i) ≥ 90 % reduction in
  scheduling-attributed cancellations vs the C2 window-scoped baseline AND (ii)
  no `local_lease_active` refusal window longer than the 180 s watchdog bound.
  On FAIL: the measured numbers are recorded, a `discovered-from` item is
  created with the offending log extract, and neither the parent nor this child
  is marked complete.
- **C4.2 — Structured result comment.** One structured result comment on the
  parent with: window bounds, precondition attestation (C1), counts + classified
  split (C3), baseline + reduction % (C2, expressed as
  `1 − live_scheduling_attributed / replay_baseline`), verdict. Cross-referenced
  from the epic `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` and from the completed sibling
  `Post-deploy 24 h prefill regression verification (LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I)` (Q2
  decision A: shared report set; sibling certified log-derived with the
  producer-accepted restart caveat, 2026-10-26T23:35Z).
- **C4.3 — Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/slot-thrashing-investigation/findings.md`
  gains the measured window + verdict and the corrected capture invocation
  (`--log` mandatory), and the 2026-10-24 numbers are labelled historical. All
  related documentation (code comments, README, docs site entries) updated to
  reflect the changes.
- **C4.4 — Test gate.** Full project test suite passes with the changes
  (executed via the test skill / dev-push gate; no ad-hoc full-suite runs).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Assemble verdict inputs: C1 attestation, C2 baseline + replay, C3 counts +
   split, and the `local_lease_active` refusal windows from the window report.
2. Apply both gates; state the verdict with the arithmetic shown.
3. Post the structured result comment; cross-reference epic + sibling.
4. Update `findings.md` (and related docs) in the worktree; build → test → commit.
5. Run the full suite via the test skill; any regression beyond scope becomes a
   `discovered-from` item, never silently fixed here.

## Dependencies

Depends on C2 and C3. Final child; satisfies parent AC6/AC8/AC9/AC10.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — watchdog/ratio thresholds (AC6 gates)
- `/tmp/ac4_window.jsonl` — C2 fixture reference

Verdict comment + cross-references, `findings.md` update, green test gate.

## Goal

Produce the measured evidence the AC3 closure verdict needs: a ≥24 h post-landing window of `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=prefill_deadline` events, with the user-traffic / audit-session split and a per-event cause attribution (occupancy / capacity / predicted-warmth), so the tracking item LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I can decide AC3(a) versus AC3(b).

## Background — the original premise is superseded by later measurement

- The scheduler epic LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG and its occupancy-aware child LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE are **completed** (commit `8b7ab7a2`, in `HEAD`; the proxy restarted with it at 2026-10-26T10:23Z).
- A later measurement on LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (window 2026-10-26 09:06 → 2026-10-27 09:06, 114 events) **falsified the second-slot head-of-line hypothesis**: 68 % of events overlapped no other prefill or decode, and `local_in_flight_requests` reached 2 in only 11 % of windows. 29 events (25 %) were "fake-warm": prompt ≈56 k, priced `new_tokens` 17–182, `eta_prefill_s` 3.7–13.8 s, cancelled at 120 s.
- The cause attributed there is predicted-but-unmeasured warmth: all 5 456 `routing_resident_prefix` decisions in that window carry `n_past_actual=none`. The fix is LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (Option D, `measured_cache_deficit` early abort), whose F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD owns the fix's own ≥24 h post-deploy measurement.
- **Do not repeat F5.** Consume its output where available and add only what the AC3 verdict needs (user/audit split, occupancy-vs-warmth attribution, per-reason counts).

## Scope

**In:** window and deploy-timestamp selection; log mining over `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`; user-traffic vs audit classification using the **same classifier** as the parent AC4 measurement (LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D); per-event attribution; a recorded dataset plus the exact commands needed to reproduce it.

**Out:** any code change (admission, deadlines, budgets, queue bounds, slot counts); the AC3 verdict itself (sibling verdict item); rewriting parent AC4. Any further admission-maths change discovered while measuring is filed as a new linked work item (`discovered-from` this item), never folded in here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Window and deploy timestamps recorded.** The ≥24 h measurement window and the deploy timestamp of every admission-affecting change inside it (at minimum `8b7ab7a2` and the Option D commit) are recorded on this item **before** measuring; any proxy restart, config reload or slot-count change inside the window is recorded as a re-base event.
- **AC2 — Parent-AC1 evidence reported.** The 22-event/7.4 h measurement (12 user-traffic) with the `progress=0` signature and the audit-load split is reported against the new window using the same classifier, so the two reports are comparable and can be referenced from the parent AC4 comment by the verdict item.
- **AC3 — Parent-AC3 counts reported.** For the window: total `reason=prefill_deadline` events, the user-traffic vs audit-session split, the hourly rate for each, and the `new_tokens` / `eta_prefill_s` / `elapsed_s` distributions — reported against both the 22-event/7.4 h baseline and the 114-event fix-item window.
- **AC4 — Cause attribution per event.** Each event is classified as **occupancy** (another session's prefill or lease in flight in the same slot pool), **capacity** (slot saturation with no other occupant) or **predicted-warmth** (large prompt, tiny priced `new_tokens`, actual prefill progress far above the priced compute), with the classification rules and evidence columns recorded. The occupancy share is the direct test of this item's original hypothesis.
- **AC5 — Conversion accounted.** `reason=measured_cache_deficit` (Option D) is reported alongside `prefill_deadline`, so a fall in one reason is never misread as the residual disappearing.
- **AC6 — Parent AC3 mapping (evidence half).** "**AC3 — Closure.** Closed only when either (a) the scheduler epic lands and a post-landing window shows zero user-traffic `prefill_deadline` evictions after acceptance, or (b) the producer explicitly re-scopes parent AC4 with an agreed threshold and the re-scoped criterion is met." — this item supplies the measured evidence for path (a) and, when (a) fails, the evidence for the (b) re-scope proposal; it does not close the tracking item.

## Key Files

- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` (window evidence)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` (existing analysis flow)
- `proxy/proxy/admission_events.py` (`log_local_eviction`, `EVICTION_REASONS` — the closed reason vocabulary)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — the post-fix window is a valid evidence window.** It is only valid if the deploy timestamps are recorded first and no admission-affecting change or slot-count change occurs inside it (AC1 re-bases the window otherwise).
- **Risk — attribution drift.** The user-traffic / audit classifier must be the parent AC4 one, or the two reports stop being comparable (AC2).
- **Risk — misreading the reason conversion.** A fall in `reason=prefill_deadline` with a rise in `reason=measured_cache_deficit` is Option D doing its job, not the residual disappearing (AC5).

## Goal (user story)

As an operator of the LLM proxy, I want the prefill-ETA admission guard to price local prefills at the rate they will actually achieve when the other slot is busy, so that admitted local dispatches convert to a first byte instead of burning the queue budget and falling back remote.

## Background / evidence (measured 2026-10-28, 23:30-00:38 + 00:00-00:38 windows)

- The local model served 15 of 1,883 streams; 1,152 routing skips and 487 admission-guard rejects occurred.
- The guard priced a 6,659-token prompt at `eta_prefill_s=13.9` (~479 t/s), yet the llama-server's own prompt-eval median is ~120 t/s (p25 85 / p75 202 / max 763, n=229 same day). Admission pricing runs 2-4x optimistic, at p95+ of the measured distribution.
- 2026-10-28 00:28:55: `decision=admit projected_wait_s=29.9 budget_s=60.0` with `busy_slots=1 in_flight_prefills=1 eta_occupancy_s=16.0`; queued the full 60 s, the gate never freed (occupant was a cold 65-89k-token audit prompt), then fell back remote — a guaranteed loss that admission was supposed to prevent. Retry was admitted again, dispatched after 13.4 s, and local immediately entered a ~480 s cooldown (dispatch failed).
- Root cause is not the gate serialisation structure (already priced as `eta * (busy_slots + 1)` plus a measured-occupant term): it is that (a) the rate calibration is unconditioned on co-residency — decode on the other slot halves prefill throughput (the single-prefill gate serialises prefills but not prefill+decode batching), and (b) the occupant-remaining term (`admitted_eta - elapsed`) inherits the optimistic rate and converges to ~0 for any occupant alive past its optimistic ETA, leaving the equally optimistic symmetric floor.

## Proposed fix

1. Maintain a separate rate distribution for contended prefills (observed while `busy_slots >= 1` / another slot generating) and price contended admissions against it; expose the chosen bucket on the decision log (e.g. `rate_bucket=contended`).
2. Rebase the occupant-remaining term on the occupant's remaining uncached new tokens priced at the contended rate, instead of `admitted_eta - elapsed`.
3. Pre/post measurement: log admission→first-byte conversion and abandoned-queue-wait share per new-token band to prove the fix.

## Scope guardrails

- Do NOT change `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60) or `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120) in this item; the ordering assertion 60 < 120 < 840 < 900 must stay intact.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A contended decision (busy_slots >= 1) is priced with the contended rate bucket; unit test asserts the bucket and that `eta_occupancy` uses the occupant's remaining new tokens at that rate, never `admitted_eta - elapsed`.
- AC2: A simulated cold occupant with 60k remaining new tokens yields `eta_occupancy` >= contended-rate x remaining; the 6,659-token / 13.9 s case now projects >= median-rate prefill (>= 55 s at 120 t/s).
- AC3: Warm-prompt admissions are unaffected (cached_ratio path unchanged).
- AC4: Post-change, the share of queued local waits ending in `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` drops below the 85% baseline measured 2026-10-19/20 over a 24 h window, with no new `local_eviction_after_acceptance` events.
- AC5: Full test suite green; existing prefill-ETA, deadline, occupancy and budget tests pass unchanged in intent.

## Related items

- LP-0MVKUKF65008D5UN Conservative prefill ETA for large prompts (percentile pricing >= 20k — the band floor this fix extends)
- LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV Prefill-ETA admission guard ignores occupancy (symmetric floor origin)
- LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE Occupancy-aware deadline admission (measured-occupant term origin)
- LP-0MVKUKEU80022C3U Deadline-aware local admission bound (120 s deadline)
- LP-0MVGR2OXT0096OGK open: Measure whether lease_state/prefill_eta predict real local contention

## Plan (LP-0MVS8T6F4006DGG3, plan_complete 2026-10-28)

Decomposed into six deliverable children in **test-first dependency order**, plus
three `idea`-stage stubs created by the AC-coverage review (each restates one
parent AC; implement as part of the named child rather than separately — see
*Coverage stubs* below).

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Covers |
|---|-------|------|-----------|--------|
| 1 | Pre-change admission-conversion baseline harness (LP-0MVS9Y7FG004QJ2S) | task | — | parent AC4 baseline (verification-first) |
| 2 | Contended prefill rate bucket (LP-0MVS9Y76R004B5M8) | feature | — | parent AC1 (bucket), AC2 (55 s case), AC3, AC5 |
| 3 | Occupant-remaining priced from new tokens at contended rate (LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ) | feature | #2 | parent AC1 (`eta_occupancy`), AC2 (60k scenario), AC5 |
| 4 | Decision-log and usage-report surface for rate_bucket (LP-0MVS9YKHL007UBBZ) | feature | #1, #2, #3 | parent AC1 (log evidence), AC4 (observability) |
| 5 | Post-change 24h measurement window vs 85% baseline (LP-0MVS9Z0GY008LCJA) | task | #1, #2, #3, #4 | parent AC4 |
| 6 | Docs and rollback for contended pricing (LP-0MVS9Z034006MFZ6) | docs | #2, #3 | parent AC5 (documented rollback) |

Dependency graph: `1 → 4 → 5`, `2 → 3 → 4`, `2 → 6`, `3 → 6`, `1 → 5`, `2 → 5`, `3 → 5`.

### Vertical-slice phasing

Every child is a minimal end-to-end slice (production code + unit tests + log/report
surface + docs where the behaviour is operator-visible). There is no horizontal
"all the parsing first" phase: child 1 lands a complete, committable measurement
tool; child 2 lands a complete calibrated bucket incl. its decision-log field;
child 3 lands the occupant re-pricing incl. its tests; child 4 makes both visible
in the standard report; child 5 proves the outcome on live traffic.

Between phases: review the next child's description against what the previous
slice actually shipped, and update its description/ACs before starting it.

### Key implementation decisions (recorded for the implementer)

- **Co-residency evidence is OR'd, not inferred.** A sample is `contended` when
  the admission-time `busy_slots >= 1` snapshot on the dispatch record says so,
  **or** another session holds a live dispatch record for the same endpoint at
  first-byte time. Both signals are deterministic in tests; no heuristics, no
  wall-clock sampling.
- **Uncalibrated contended window falls back to the solitary window** and logs
  `rate_bucket=solitary_fallback`. Rationale: the guard's founding rule is
  "never reject on a guess"; a guessed contended slowdown multiplier would
  violate it. The log field makes the residual optimism visible instead.
- **Occupant rebase is token-based, not time-decayed**: `progress =
  min(1, elapsed / eta_prefill_s)`, `remaining_new = new_tokens * (1 - progress)`,
  `remaining_s = estimate(remaining_new, cached_ratio=0, contended=True)`.
  Records lacking `new_tokens`/`eta_prefill_s` contribute 0.0 (fail-open,
  byte-for-byte today's behaviour).
- **No new config knobs in this item**; the contended window reuses
  `local_admission_guard_min_samples`, and the documented rollback stays
  `local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off`.
- **Guardrails untouched**: `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60) and
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120); the `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` ordering
  assertion must keep passing.

### Coverage stubs (created by the AC-coverage review)

`LP-0MVSA3WOA002NAUH` (parent AC1), `LP-0MVSA3WWI00058T9` (parent AC3),
`LP-0MVSA3X5B008ZA88` (parent AC4) restate parent ACs whose wording differs from
the child ACs that cover them (coverage review matched them at 0.34/0.24/0.36).
They are **absorbed**: AC1 → children #2 and #3, AC3 → child #2 AC5, AC4 →
children #1 and #5. Do not implement them as separate work; close each as
absorbed when its covering child is complete.

### Effort and risk

Re-estimated after decomposition (supersedes the pre-plan `Extra Small` /
0.00 h placeholder estimate): **Medium effort, 21.6 h expected (range
20.0-42.0 h, 29.6 h recommended with overheads)**, risk **Medium (10/25)**,
confidence 85 %. The pre-plan estimate carried O=M=P=0.00 h (a degenerate
three-point input) and was not usable for scheduling.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Interview outcome: **no blocking questions** — the intake brief already specified
the goal, the three-part fix, the scope guardrails (60/120 unchanged) and five
testable ACs, and the six-child decomposition follows directly from them. Two
non-blocking questions are recorded for the operator; neither blocks
implementation.

- **OPEN QUESTION (directed to the operator, non-blocking) — AC4 is
  time-blocked.** Parent AC4 requires a 24 h *post-change* window. Decomposed as
  child #5 (LP-0MVS9Z0GY008LCJA), which can only run after the fix is deployed
  and a day of traffic has elapsed. Assumption recorded: parent AC4 is satisfied
  by child #5's committed measurement record, not by the implementation commits.
  Preferred option: **keep AC4 in this parent, gated by child #5**. Alternative:
  move AC4 wholesale into a follow-up measurement item and close the parent on
  AC1-AC3 + AC5. Source: this planning session; evidence: parent description,
  AC4 vs the `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` baseline of 2026-10-19/20.
  Research: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` and
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` show no existing per-band
  conversion metric, hence child #1 lands the harness before any estimator change.
- **OPEN QUESTION (directed to the operator, non-blocking) — definition of
  "contended".** The plan defines a contended sample as *any* local prefill
  observed while another session holds a slot (prefill or decode), matching the
  measured mechanism (decode on the other slot halves prefill throughput).
  Preferred option: **co-residency (any other live slot holder)**, because the
  measured 2-4x gap is a batching effect, not a prefill-vs-prefill serialisation
  effect. Alternative: restrict the contended window to "another *prefill* is in
  flight". Source: this planning session; evidence: parent background —
  `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` serialises prefills, so prefill+prefill
  contention is already excluded by the gate, leaving prefill+decode as the
  observed contention. Research: `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
  (`_get_live_prefill_in_flight_count`, `_live_prefill_remaining_seconds`) and
  `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`_local_gate_occupancy`).

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-28 (plan session `herdr-1793200851-672483-3216`): six children created

# Feature: preference vocabulary — add `local-preferred`, alias `local-only`

Parent: LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY. Depends-on: none. Depended-on-by: LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ, LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE, LP-0MVSHXTX1007D58Z.

## Problem statement

The proxy's `X-Local-Preference` vocabulary is defined three times over — a
canonical table in `admission_reserve.py` plus hand-rolled copies in
`priority.py` and `provider.py` — and its only "pin local" value is the
absolute `local-only`. The parent epic replaces `local-only` with
`local-preferred` (defer while local-capable, remote once the prompt outgrows
local capacity), but every downstream behaviour change is unimplementable
until the wire vocabulary itself is widened and the alias accepted. Without
this item, changing the vocabulary would silently break deployed herdr
workers that still send `local-only`, and the three parsers would keep
drifting apart.

## Users

- As a **proxy maintainer**, I want one canonical definition of the preference
  vocabulary so a new value is added in exactly one place and both routing
  cycles agree by construction.
- As a **deployed herdr worker** still sending `X-Local-Preference: local-only`,
  I want my existing header accepted and normalised, so upgrading the proxy does
  not break my dispatches.
- As a **sibling-item implementer** (LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ / LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE),
  I want `local-preferred` to already parse to a stable constant, so the
  deferral semantics land on top of the vocabulary instead of re-inventing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** `admission_reserve.parse_preference({"x-local-preference": "local-preferred"}) == "local-preferred"`, and `parse_preference({"x-local-preference": "local-only"}) == "local-preferred"` (alias normalised).
- **AC2** Sending the legacy alias emits exactly one deprecation log line per request (level `WARNING`, naming both `local-only` and `local-preferred`), not one per skip/refusal line within that request.
- **AC3** Header lookup stays case-insensitive (`Local-Only`, `LOCAL-PREFERRED` both accepted) and unknown values / absent header keep falling back to `prefer-local` with no behaviour change versus today (LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL AC8).
- **AC4** Exactly one preference parser and one set of preference constants exist in the codebase: `priority.py` and `provider.py` import them from `admission_reserve.py`; no second `VALID_PREFERENCES` tuple, no second local `"local-only"` / `"remote-ok"` literal used for a routing comparison.
- **AC5** Behaviour is unchanged at every comparison site: after normalisation, `local-only` and `local-preferred` clients are still treated as *pin-local* by the existing choke points and refusal builders (terminal 429, never a silent fall-through). Deferral semantics remain out of scope here.
- **AC6** Tests cover the four vocabulary cases — `local-preferred` parses, mixed-case alias normalises, unknown value → `prefer-local`, absent header → `prefer-local` — plus the once-per-request deprecation, and pass under the changed-scope gate (`/skill:test --scope changed`).
- **AC7** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, docstrings, the `proxy/docs/routing.md` `X-Local-Preference` table (new canonical value + legacy-alias note) and the `proxy/config.yaml` preference commentary.
- **AC8** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No semantic change in this item.** The verdict split (deferrable vs
  too-large-for-local), the deferral path and the retryable-429 timing belong
  to LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ and LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE. This item must leave every
  routing outcome byte-identical for all four wire values.
- **Wire compatibility is mandatory.** `local-only` must never become an
  unknown value: that would demote deployed clients to `prefer-local` and let
  their requests go remote behind their back — a contract violation of
  LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL AC4 and of LP-0MVRMC1L3006F0F3's choke point.
- **One source of truth.** The alias must be expressed as a constant, not as
  string literals sprinkled at call sites; AC4 is enforced by review and by the
  "no second literal" test.
- **No client-side work.** herdr `LocalPreference` plumbing and Worklog header
  injection are out of scope (owned by the ContextHub store).
- **Documentation boundary.** `proxy/docs/routing.md` gains only the vocabulary
  row and the wire-compat note; the full `local-preferred` semantics prose is
  LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57's deliverable, so this item must not pre-empt it.
- **Scope creep guard.** Any further opportunity discovered while implementing
  (e.g. a stale `local_only` token in observability, a metrics label) is
  recorded as a new linked work item rather than absorbed here.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py:56-63` — `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY`, `PREF_PREFER_LOCAL`, `PREF_REMOTE_OK`, `VALID_PREFERENCES`, `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE`, `HEADER_PREFERENCE`. `parse_preference()` at :468 does lower-case lookup on `x-local-preference` / `X-Local-Preference`, returns `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE` for missing/unknown, and logs `logger.debug` for unknown values.
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py:388-407` — `local_preference_for_request()` re-imports `parse_preference`, caches on `request._local_preference`, and hard-codes `"prefer-local"` as its exception fallback. `apply_local_preference()` at :409 compares the raw literal `"remote-ok"`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:6441-6462` — duplicate `_PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` / `_PREF_REMOTE_OK` constants and a duplicate `_request_local_preference()` doing the same import-and-cache dance with the same `"prefer-local"` fallback literal.
- Comparison sites on the duplicate constant: `provider.py:6698` (dispatch-loop choke point), `:7106` (admission-refusal path), `:11460` (remote-fallback cycle); `_PREF_REMOTE_OK` at `:9947` and `:10612`.
- `proxy/config.yaml:1925-1930` — preference commentary documenting `prefer-local|local-only|remote-ok`.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md:1201-1213` — `X-Local-Preference` table with `prefer-local` / `local-only` / `remote-ok` rows.
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py:386` — `test_unknown_preference_value_falls_back_to_prefer_local` already pins the unknown/absent/`remote-ok` cases; the alias and `local-preferred` cases are missing.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` and `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` send `x-local-preference: local-only` throughout, so they become the de-facto alias-compatibility suite.

## Desired change

1. `admission_reserve.py` becomes the vocabulary's single source of truth:
   - add `PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED = "local-preferred"`;
   - retain `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY = "local-only"` as the documented legacy alias, in a
     dedicated alias table (e.g. `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES = {PREF_LOCAL_ONLY: PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED}`)
     so the canonical set and the alias set cannot drift;
   - `VALID_PREFERENCES` accepts `local-preferred`; `parse_preference()`
     normalises the alias after the lower-case lookup and emits the
     once-per-request deprecation;
   - keep case-insensitive header lookup and the unknown → `prefer-local`
     fallback verbatim.
2. `priority.py` and `provider.py` delete their local constants and their
   duplicate parsers, importing the canonical constants/parser instead; every
   comparison keeps comparing against the canonical pin-local value so
   normalised `local-only` traffic still hits the same choke points (AC5).
3. Docs/commentary: `config.yaml` preference block and the
   `proxy/docs/routing.md` table describe `local-preferred` as canonical with
   `local-only` accepted as a deprecated alias.
4. Tests: extend `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` with the four
   vocabulary cases plus the once-per-request deprecation assertion, and add a
   guard test that fails if a second preference literal/parser reappears
   outside `admission_reserve.py`.

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-10-28)

**Decomposition decision: no child items — one vertical slice.**
The deliverable is a single behaviour-preserving vocabulary change: canonical
constants + alias normalisation + parser consolidation + the affected comparison
sites + docs + tests, landing in one commit. Splitting it into children would slice
by *layer* (vocabulary / consolidation / docs / tests), which the plan skill forbids
(vertical slices only); the whole slice is ~9.5 h (Small / Medium) and fits one
implement session. Test-first is honoured *within* the item by the step order below.
Approval pause not required (effort Small, risk Medium — not XL + High/Severe).

### Target outcome

`local-preferred` is the canonical pin-local value, parsed by one parser;
`local-only` is accepted and normalised to it with exactly one deprecation warning
per request; every routing outcome stays byte-identical for all four wire values.

### Definition of done (pass/fail checks)

- New/extended assertions in `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` pass, and the
  single-source guard test passes (see *Enforcement of AC4*).
- `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`, `test_local_admission_guard.py`,
  `test_local_fallback_reason_tokens.py`, `test_hard_routing_cap.py` and
  `test_startup_ramp.py` pass **unmodified** — they are the legacy-alias
  compatibility proof for AC5.
- `/skill:test --scope changed` green; full suite green at the dev-push gate (AC8).

### Implementation sequence (test-first)

1. **Red — vocabulary tests** in `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`:
   `test_local_preferred_parses`, `test_legacy_local_only_alias_normalises`
   (including mixed case `Local-Only`), extend
   `test_unknown_preference_value_falls_back_to_prefer_local` with the
   absent-header and `purple` cases, plus
   `test_legacy_alias_logs_one_deprecation_per_request` (caplog at `WARNING`: call
   `provider._request_local_preference(req)` twice and
   `priority.local_preference_for_request(req)` once on one request object; assert
   exactly one record, its level, and that its text names both `local-only` and
   `local-preferred`).
   → verify: `/skill:test --scope changed` fails only on the new assertions.
2. **Green — vocabulary** in `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`: add
   `PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED = "local-preferred"`; keep `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` as the
   documented legacy alias; add
   `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES = {PREF_LOCAL_ONLY: PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED}`; widen
   `VALID_PREFERENCES` to the canonical set; in `parse_preference()` normalise via
   `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES.get(value, value)` after the lower-case lookup and emit
   one `logger.warning` naming both tokens. Keep the case-insensitive
   `x-local-preference` / `X-Local-Preference` lookup and the unknown →

# Feature: capacity verdict — deferrable vs too-large-for-local

Parent: LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY.

## Goal

One authoritative classification of *why* the local route cannot serve a request right now, so chain selection can distinguish "wait, a slot is coming" from "this prompt will never fit local".

## Deliverables

- A single verdict helper (e.g. `local_capacity_verdict(...)`) in the admission/reserve module, consumed by both dispatch cycles and the refusal builder — derived from the existing estimator/guard decision and the local provider's configured limits, **not** a second ETA or token-estimation implementation.
- Verdict vocabulary:
  - `deferrable` — prompt is inside the local serving envelope; the blocking reason is temporal (`eta_exceeds_budget_direct`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`, queue/occupancy, lease denial, busy slots, stall/cooldown).
  - `too_large` — prompt exceeds the local serving envelope: context above the local model's limit/`cold_threshold` verdict, or `new_tokens > local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` (`prefill_budget_exceeded`).
- The verdict (and the underlying reason token) appears in the 429 payload and in a dedicated log line, so a deferral is never mistaken for chain exhaustion (relates to LP-0MVNTJQVB007QWEZ and LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ).
- Unit tests for the classification table.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 `deferrable` is returned for the observed incident shape (`eta_prefill_s=31.7`, `projected_wait_s=63.4`, `budget_s=60.0`, `new_tokens=6627`, `budget_tokens=25000`).
- AC2 `too_large` is returned when `new_tokens > local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens`, and when the local context check already skips the local route for size.
- AC3 Exactly one implementation is used by both dispatch cycles and the refusal builder (assert by import/call-site review, not by duplicated logic).
- AC4 The verdict is observable: refusal body carries it and one log line states preference + verdict + reason.
- AC5 Table-driven unit tests cover deferrable, too-large (both triggers) and non-guard temporal reasons.
- AC6 All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and docstrings; operator-facing docs (`docs/`, `proxy/config.yaml` commentary) are tracked in LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57.
- AC7 Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes

Do not pre-empt the retry-timing contract (LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X) — this item only classifies; timing stays in `_refusal_retry_timing`.

Classification inputs come from the existing estimator/guard decision and the configured envelope (`local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens`, local context limit); no second ETA, token-estimation or sizing model is introduced (parent assumption A1).

## Constraints

- One helper, imported by both dispatch cycles and the refusal builder — a duplicated verdict in `provider.py` violates AC3.
- Verdict values are exactly `deferrable` and `too_large`; an unclassifiable case must default to the existing pin-local refusal (fail safe: never promote a fits-local request to remote).
- No retry-timing change, no queue or lease behaviour change, no config default change.
- `prefer-local` and `remote-ok` behaviour is untouched by the verdict.

# Feature: local-preferred chain selection and deferral

Parent: LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY.

## Goal

Make `local-preferred` behave as "local-only while deferrable, remote-ok once the prompt is too large for local", on every exit path of both dispatch cycles.

## Deliverables

1. **Local-pinned while deferrable.** `apply_local_preference()` and the dispatch-loop choke point (`_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote`, both cycles) treat `local-preferred` exactly as today's `local-only`: no non-local dispatch on any exit — admission refusal, lease denial, slot exhaustion, context/`resident_prefix` skip, stall, empty response, sibling-failure.
2. **Deferral.** A deferrable request with no free local slot queues within `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`; on expiry it returns a **retryable** 429 via the existing truthful-timing helper (`_refusal_retry_timing`): `retryable: true`, `Retry-After`, `retry_at`, `X-Local-Route: refused`, plus the verdict from LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ. The request is *not* enqueued twice, no lease/slot is leaked, the response is stamped once.
3. **Too-large → remote-ok.** When the verdict is `too_large`, remove the local entry from the effective chain at resolution time (the existing `remote-ok` filtering path) so remote tiers serve the request with no deferral and no local-capacity 429.
4. **Alias.** `local-only` normalises to the same behaviour (LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16), including log lines.
5. **Logging.** One line per request naming the resolved preference and whether it was pinned, deferred or promoted to remote — so an operator can tell a deferral from chain exhaustion.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 With `local-preferred` and a deferrable verdict on *each* listed exit path, no remote dispatch occurs (asserted per path in tests).
- AC2 With `local-preferred` and a free local slot, the request is served locally as today.
- AC3 With `local-preferred` and a deferrable verdict after the queue budget, the response is 429 with `retryable: true`, a `Retry-After`/`retry_at` pair consistent with the refusal timing contract, `X-Local-Route: refused`, and a body verdict of `deferrable`.
- AC4 With `local-preferred` and a `too_large` verdict, the chain excludes local and a remote provider serves the request; no 429 is produced for local capacity.
- AC5 Requires no change to response shape for `prefer-local` / `remote-ok` / remote-less chains.
- AC6 No queue-depth, lease or slot leak and no double header stamping on any of the above (asserted in tests).
- AC7 All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and docstrings; operator-facing docs (`docs/`, `proxy/config.yaml` commentary) are tracked in LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57.
- AC8 Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Never promote a fits-local request.** The only path to a paid provider is the `too_large` verdict (parent assumption A2); a deferrable request that exhausts the queue is refused with a retryable 429, never silently promoted.
- **Never defer a too-large request.** `too_large` removes local from the chain before any queueing (AC4).
- **Queue bounds unchanged:** `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60 s) and `contention_queue_max_depth` keep their current values; no new config default is introduced.
- **Truthful retry timing:** `Retry-After` / `retry_at` come from the existing `_refusal_retry_timing()` helper (LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X) — this item does not renegotiate the retry contract.
- **No double enqueue / no double stamping:** a deferred request is enqueued exactly once and the response is stamped exactly once; leases and slots are always released.
- **Single preference source:** all comparisons use the canonical constants/parser from `admission_reserve.py` (LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16) — no second literal.
- **Remote-less chains** (`private` model) keep deferring and never promote (parent assumption A5).
- **Scope guard:** richer queue UX (priority promotion, lease-grace tuning) belongs to LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R, not here.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py:387` `local_preference_for_request()`, `:410` `apply_local_preference()` — chain filtering.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:4483` `_refusal_retry_timing()`, `:6445` `_request_local_preference()`, `:6663` `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` (choke point comparing at `:6698`), the admission-refusal comparison at `:7106`, the remote-fallback comparison at `:11460`, and both dispatch cycles (`:9947` / `:10612` `remote-ok` filtering).
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`, `proxy/proxy/router.py` — bounded queue and dispatch.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — the existing exit-path matrices this item must extend.

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — preference constants/parser (consumed) and the verdict helper (consumed) feeding the pinned/deferred/promoted branch.
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py` — the existing wait budget/depth used for deferral; no new queue implementation.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — per-exit-path no-remote-dispatch assertions and the retryable-429 field assertions.

# Test: local-preferred behaviour matrix

Parent: LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY.

## Goal

Pin the whole contract in one table-driven regression suite so future routing work cannot silently revert to "hard 429" or "silent remote".

## Matrix

| Preference | Slot | Verdict | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| absent / `prefer-local` | free | — | local (unchanged) |
| absent / `prefer-local` | busy | deferrable | remote fallback (unchanged) |
| `remote-ok` | — | — | local removed from chain, remote serves (unchanged) |
| `local-preferred` | free | — | local |
| `local-preferred` | busy | deferrable | queue → retryable 429, **no** remote dispatch |
| `local-preferred` | busy | too_large | remote serves, **no** local-capacity 429 |
| `local-only` (legacy) | busy | deferrable | identical to `local-preferred` |
| any | — | remote-less chain (`private` model) | unchanged |

## Deliverables

- Extend `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (rename semantics or add a sibling file) and `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` with the matrix above.
- Each row asserts: HTTP status, `X-Local-Route`, `X-Provider` / served entry, the presence or absence of remote dispatch (spy on `proxy_to_remote`), and for deferrals the retry fields.
- A named regression reproducing the 2026-10-28 incident numbers (`eta_prefill_s=31.7`, `projected_wait_s=63.4`, `budget_s=60.0`, `new_tokens=6627`, `budget_tokens=25000`) asserting `deferrable` + retryable 429 + zero remote calls.

| Matrix row | Home | Additional assertions |
|---|---|---|
| absent / `prefer-local`, free | `test_admission_reserve.py` (vocabulary rows) + `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (existing exit rows) | `X-Local-Route: local`, local provider name in `X-Provider`, zero remote calls; response shape byte-identical to today (no `retryable`, no `verdict` field) |
| absent / `prefer-local`, busy, deferrable | `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (existing exit rows) | remote provider serves, `X-Local-Route: remote`, local neither dispatched nor refused |
| `remote-ok`, any | `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (`test_remote_ok_still_strips_local_entries`) | local entry absent from the resolved chain (`apply_local_preference` output), remote serves |
| `local-preferred`, free | `test_local_admission_guard.py` (`_free_slot_cfg`) | served locally, `X-Local-Route: local`, no queue entry, no 429 |
| `local-preferred`, busy, deferrable | `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (preference axis on every exit row) + `test_local_admission_guard.py` | 429, `X-Local-Route: refused`, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` set, `retryable: true`, `Retry-After`/`retry_at` pair, body verdict `deferrable`, **zero** `proxy_to_remote` calls |

# Feature: capacity-verdict wiring — dispatch cycles, refusal body and log line

Parent: LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ. Depends on LP child A ("`local_capacity_verdict` helper and classification table").

## Goal

Make the single verdict helper the only source of the classification at every local-route exit, and make the verdict observable: it appears in the 429 refusal body and in exactly one log line, so a deferral is never mistaken for chain exhaustion.

## Deliverables

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`:
  - Both dispatch cycles and the refusal builder (`_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` / `_build_local_only_refusal_response()`, call sites of the existing local-only choke point) obtain the verdict **only** by calling `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)`; no verdict re-derivation, no second reason table.
  - `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` adds `"verdict": "deferrable" | "too_large"` to the 429 JSON body, alongside the existing `reason`, `retryable` and timing fields. No header is added (wire-header work belongs to LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57 if wanted).
  - One log line per classified refusal, e.g. `local_capacity_verdict preference=<pref> verdict=<verdict> reason=<reason>` — emitted exactly once per request, not per skip branch.
  - Retry timing stays entirely in `_refusal_retry_timing()`; this item classifies and reports, it does **not** change timing, queueing, lease or slot behaviour, and it does not implement remote promotion on `too_large` (that is LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE).
- Tests:
  - `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` (or a focused addition) / `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`: a spy/patch test that replaces `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict` and asserts it is called from **both** dispatch cycles and from the refusal builder (asserts the single-implementation contract, AC3 here).
  - Refusal-body assertions for `verdict: deferrable` (incident shape: `eta_prefill_s=31.7`, `projected_wait_s=63.4`, `budget_s=60.0`) and `verdict: too_large` (`prefill_budget_exceeded`), keeping the existing status/`Retry-After`/`X-Local-Route` expectations intact.
  - A `caplog` assertion that exactly one verdict log line is emitted per refusal and that it names preference + verdict + reason.
  - Update `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` expectations where the body gained `verdict` (existing assertions stay, only extended).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 Exactly one implementation is used by both dispatch cycles and the refusal builder (assert by import/call-site review, not by duplicated logic): a patch/spy test proves each call site routes through `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict`.
- AC2 A deferrable refusal returns 429 with body `verdict: "deferrable"`, `reason` unchanged, `X-Local-Route: refused`, and the retry timing exactly as `_refusal_retry_timing` already produced it (no timing change; incident shape advertises a retryable wait).
- AC3 A too-large refusal returns 429 with body `verdict: "too_large"` and the existing `reason` (`prefill_budget_exceeded` or `context_too_large`).
- AC4 The verdict is observable: refusal body carries it and one log line states preference + verdict + reason (asserted with `caplog`; exactly one line per refusal, not per skip branch).
- AC5 `prefer-local` and `remote-ok` behaviour is unchanged (existing tests keep passing), and no `local-only`/`local-preferred` promotion to remote is introduced here.
- AC6 Comments and docstrings are updated at every call site that now consults the verdict.
- AC7 Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (changed-scope gate first; the full suite is enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- Import the helper; never copy its rules (`provider.py` must not contain a verdict `if reason in (...)` table).
- Fail-safe preserved: an unclassifiable exit still pins the request to local (today's refusal) — no accidental promotion to a paid provider.
- No retry-timing change (`_refusal_retry_timing` untouched), no queue/lease behaviour change, no config-default change, no double header stamping.
- Verdict is additive in the 429 body; no existing field is renamed or removed.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — both dispatch cycles (choke-point call sites), `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()`, `_build_local_only_refusal_response()`, the single verdict log line.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — imported helper (delivered by LP child A; read-only here).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — refusal-body and log-line assertions for deferrable/too-large.

# Feature: `local-preferred` pin across every local-route exit

Parent: LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE. Depends on: LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 (preference vocabulary — canonical `PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED`, alias normalisation) and LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ (capacity verdict feature, incl. its children LP-0MVSL7QJW006OYPB `local_capacity_verdict()` and LP-0MVSL7SDV007XVG6 wiring).

## Goal

A `local-preferred` request whose capacity verdict is `deferrable` is never handed to a non-local provider, whichever way the local route exits — admission refusal, lease denial, slot exhaustion, context/`resident_prefix` skip, stall, empty response or sibling-failure — on **both** dispatch cycles. This is today's `local-only` guarantee, expressed on the new canonical value and gated by the verdict instead of by the raw header value.

This slice is the *pin* half of the parent feature: it decides **whether** a non-local dispatch may happen. Deferral (queue-budget expiry → retryable 429) is LP child "deferral"; chain-level stripping of local on `too_large` and the promoted log line are LP child "too-large promotion"; the single per-request outcome line is LP child "routing-outcome line".

## Deliverables

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`:
  - One request-scoped pin predicate (e.g. `_local_preference_pins_local(request, preference) -> bool`) returning `True` only when the resolved preference is the canonical pin-local constant **and** `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)` is **not** `too_large`. `prefer-local` / `remote-ok` / absent → `False`; `too_large` → `False` (the request must fall through, never be refused).
  - `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` (~:6686) — replace the raw `preference != _PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` comparison with the predicate, at **both** call sites (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` ~:10057, `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` ~:10742). Docstring reworded from "local-only choke point" to "pin-local choke point" naming `local-preferred` (the alias is already normalised upstream, so one branch covers both wire values).
  - The admission-refusal comparison in `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` (~:7130, `return ("refused_local_only", ...)`) uses the predicate, so a deferrable `local-preferred` request returns the existing refusal instead of `admission_reject` fall-through, while a `too_large` request keeps the `admission_reject` fall-through with **no** 429.
  - The remote-fallback / direct-guard comparison in the `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` free-slot path (~:11460 region, `eta_exceeds_budget_direct`) is audited and routed through the same predicate — no third hand-rolled comparison.
  - No new refusal construction: the refusal keeps coming from `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` / `_refusal_retry_timing()` unchanged (the body `verdict` field arrives with LP-0MVSL7SDV007XVG6).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — extend `_EXIT_ROWS` coverage with a `local-preferred` parameterisation. Every row asserts its **own** outcome (no shared assertion):
  - deferrable-classified rows (`thrash_cooldown`, `router_skip_economic`, `router_skip_residency`, `router_skip_tenancy`, `queue_depth_cap`, `queue_wait_expiry`, `admission_guard_free_slot`, `quota_hard_stop`, `chain_cooldown`, `no_local_route`) → `calls == []`, 429, `X-Local-Route: refused`, header reason token and body `reason` agreeing;
  - too-large-classified rows (`router_skip_physical_cap` `context_too_large`, `entry_context_cap`) → `calls == ["remote"]`, 200, no refusal code (parent AC4 boundary; see AC4);
  - **post-dispatch exits** (parent AC1's "slot exhaustion, stall, empty response, sibling-failure"): new rows whose local dispatch *is* attempted once and then fails — slot exhaustion (`slot_info` / 409 lease-active), lease denial after the lease wait (`_lease_action == "fallback"` / `"refused_local_only"`), GPU OOM, `model_loading`, local error status, empty local response (`_is_empty_response`), stall-after-content and sibling/domain failure — each asserting `calls.count("local") == 1`, no `"remote"` in `calls`, 429 with `X-Local-Route: refused` and the recorded reason token. These exits `continue` to the loop head where the choke point decides, so the row proves the structural guarantee rather than assuming it.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — a free-slot case: `local-preferred` + free local slot + admitting guard → served locally, no refusal (parent AC2).
- Comments/docstrings at every touched comparison site.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 (parent AC1) With `local-preferred` and a deferrable verdict on each listed exit path, no remote dispatch occurs (asserted per path in tests): pre-dispatch matrix rows assert `calls == []` and post-dispatch local-failure rows assert one local attempt only; every refusal is 429 with `X-Local-Route: refused` and its stable reason token (header and body agreeing), asserted per row with the row's own failure message.
- AC2 (parent AC2) With `local-preferred`, a free local slot and an admitting guard, the request is served locally: `calls == ["local"]`, 200, `X-Local-Route: local`, no 429.
- AC3 The pin decision has exactly one implementation: a test asserts both `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote` call sites and the admission-refusal path consult the same predicate, and that the predicate reads the canonical `admission_reserve` constants and `local_capacity_verdict()` (a spy/patch proves the helper is the only verdict source — no `if reason in (...)` table in `provider.py`).
- AC4 A `too_large` request is **never** refused by this path: the two size rows dispatch remote with `calls == ["remote"]` and 200, and no local-capacity 429 body is produced. (Chain-level stripping and the promoted log line belong to LP child "too-large promotion"; this AC pins only "no refusal".)
- AC5 (parent AC5) Requires no change to response shape for `prefer-local` / `remote-ok` / remote-less chains: the existing matrix rows pass **unmodified**, and every anchored response keeps its headers/body apart from the additive `verdict` field delivered by LP-0MVSL7SDV007XVG6.
- AC6 (parent AC6) No queue-depth, lease or slot leak and no double header stamping on any of the above (asserted in tests): each refusal carries `X-Local-Route` exactly once and `contention_queue.queue_depth() == 0` after the request, with no lease left registered for the session.
- AC7 (parent AC7) Comments and docstrings updated at every touched comparison site and in the refusal builder; operator-facing docs (`proxy/docs/`, `proxy/config.yaml` commentary) remain out of scope — tracked in LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57.
- AC8 (parent AC8) Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (the changed-scope gate `/skill:test --scope changed` first; the full suite is enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- **Never promote a fits-local request.** A `deferrable` request that cannot run now is refused/deferred, never silently moved to a paid provider (parent assumption A2).
- **Never refuse a too-large request** for local capacity; it falls through (parent AC4). Do not implement chain stripping here.
- **Single preference source:** compare against `admission_reserve.PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED` (and the verdict constants); no `"local-only"` / `"local-preferred"` literal comparison in `provider.py` (LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 AC4 stays enforced).
- **Single verdict source:** `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict()`; no re-derived classification.
- **Untouched:** `_refusal_retry_timing()`, queue bounds (`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`, `contention_queue_max_depth`), config defaults, response field names.
- **Fail-safe direction:** an unclassifiable exit stays pinned (helper returns `deferrable`), so an unknown reason can never promote to remote.
- Scope guard: no queue UX work (LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R), no client-side herdr/pi work.

## Existing state (verified during planning)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:6686` `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote(request, provider_cfg, model_config, config, preference)`; pin comparison today is `if preference != _PREF_LOCAL_ONLY: return None`, `_PREF_LOCAL_ONLY = "local-only"` at :6440 (removed by LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16).
- Call sites of the choke point: `:10057` (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`, defined :9901) and `:10742` (`_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`, defined :10572) — immediately after `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions` and before every `continue`/dispatch.
- Admission refusal: `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` returns `("refused_local_only", _admission.reason, None)` at `:7130` when `_request_local_preference(request) == _PREF_LOCAL_ONLY`; the free-slot guard's `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` handling lives in `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` around :11440-11480.

- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` (1704 lines) already exercises the guard-refusal path with `local-only`; the free-slot local-serve case is the AC2 addition.

# Feature: one routing-outcome line per request

Parent: LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE. Depends on: LP children "local-preferred pin across every local-route exit", "deferral — queue-budget expiry yields a retryable 429" and "too-large promotion — local stripped from the effective chain" (each stamps its outcome).

## Goal

Every request emits exactly **one** log line naming the resolved preference and whether it was pinned to local, deferred, promoted to remote (or served/exhausted), so an operator can tell a deferral from chain exhaustion without correlating per-skip lines — and a legacy `local-only` request is reported under its normalised value.

## Deliverables

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`:
  - A single emission point on the top-level return path — `_stamp_local_route_headers()` (~:6608), which both entries (`proxy_with_fallback` :12550, `proxy_with_remote_fallback` :10455) already call exactly once after `_run_chain_cycles()` — emitting:
    `local_preference_resolved preference=<resolved> outcome=<pinned|deferred|promoted|local|remote|exhausted> reason=<token|none> session=<id> model=<name>`
  - Outcome stamped on the request at the existing decision points: pin refusal (`pinned`), deferral refusal (`deferred`), pre-loop strip (`promoted`), local success (`local`), remote success (`remote`), exhaustion (`exhausted`). A request that resolves `prefer-local`/`remote-ok` reports the preference verbatim with the actual serving outcome.
  - Emission is best-effort (`try/except`, `logger.info`) and must never raise or mutate the response; it must be outside the per-cycle loop so a chain-hold retry (multiple `_run_chain_cycles` iterations) still produces exactly one line.
  - The resolved preference is the **normalised** value already cached on the request (`request._local_preference`), so `local-only` prints as `local-preferred` (alias parity with LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16).
- Tests (`proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` and/or `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`):
  - `caplog` assertions per outcome: local served, pinned refusal, deferred refusal, promoted remote, `prefer-local` remote fall-through, legacy `local-only` → normalised line. Each asserts **count == 1** for the line, its preference field, its outcome field and its reason token.
  - A multi-cycle chain-hold case asserting still exactly one line.
- Comments/docstring at `_stamp_local_route_headers()` describing the single-emission contract and why the outcome is stamped rather than logged at each branch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 Exactly one `local_preference_resolved` line per request on every outcome — asserted with `caplog` for: local served, pinned refusal, deferred refusal, promoted remote, `prefer-local` remote success and exhaustion (count == 1 each).
- AC2 The line names the **resolved** preference and the outcome (`pinned` / `deferred` / `promoted` / `local` / `remote` / `exhausted`) plus the canonical reason token when one exists, so a deferral (`outcome=deferred reason=fallback_after_queue`) is unambiguously distinguishable from chain exhaustion (`outcome=exhausted`) — the parent-epic log requirement (LP-0MVNTJQVB007QWEZ) and never "All providers exhausted" for a deferral (LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ).
- AC3 A legacy `X-Local-Preference: local-only` request logs `preference=local-preferred` and never presents `local-only` as the resolved value (alias parity; the once-per-request deprecation warning from LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 is unchanged and separate).
- AC4 Emission cannot change behaviour: a test asserts the response status, headers and body are identical with the line suppressed, and that an exception inside the emission (patched logger) still returns the response unchanged.
- AC5 Exactly one line even when `_run_chain_cycles()` performs multiple chain-hold cycles for one request.
- AC6 No competing per-skip outcome lines: the existing `priority_routing`, `local_admission_guard`, `contention_queue_*` and `local_only_refused` lines are left as they are (asserted unchanged), and no new line is emitted inside either dispatch loop.
- AC7 (parent AC7) All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and docstrings; operator-facing docs (`docs/`, `proxy/config.yaml` commentary) are tracked in LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57.
- AC8 (parent AC8) Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (changed-scope gate first; the full suite is enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- One line per **request**, not per cycle, per skip branch or per refusal builder.
- No new observability vocabulary: outcome values are a small closed set defined beside the existing preference constants (or in `provider.py` next to the refusal helpers); reason tokens come from the existing canonical table.
- No metrics/OTel/HTTP-header addition — log line only.
- Best-effort and side-effect free: observability must never break or alter a response.
- Scope guard: no refusal-line redesign (LP-0MVRMC275000R2W6 owns the refusal lines), no operator docs (LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57).

## Existing state (verified during planning)

- `_stamp_local_route_headers(response, request, model_config)` at `proxy/provider.py:6608` — the existing single choke point on the top-level return path (docstring: "Single choke point on the top-level return path so local success, remote success, refusal and exhaustion are all covered"). It delegates to `admission_reserve.stamp_route_headers()` and reads `request._local_fallback_reason`; a response already carrying `X-Local-Route` is left untouched. Both entries call it once after `_run_chain_cycles()` (:10488 `proxy_with_remote_fallback`, :12583 `proxy_with_fallback`), so it is the only place where exactly-once emission is structural.
- `request._local_preference` is the cached normalised preference (set by `provider._request_local_preference()` / `priority.local_preference_for_request()`); `request._local_fallback_reason` is the canonical reason token stamped by `_note_local_fallback_reason()`.
- `_run_chain_cycles(request, path, model_config, config, cycle_fn)` (:9797) runs chain-hold retry cycles, which is why per-cycle logging would duplicate.
- Existing per-request lines an operator already correlates: `priority_routing ... preference=<pref>` (both cycles), `local_admission_guard decision=... reason=...`, `contention_queue_wait`/`contention_queue_dispatch`/`contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`, `local_only_refused reason=<token> preference=...` (`_log_local_only_refusal()` ~:6505).
- Tests today assert on those lines with `caplog` in `test_routing_preference_logging.py` (786 lines) — the natural home for the new-line assertions alongside `test_local_admission_guard.py`.

## Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — outcome stamping in both cycles plus the refusal paths, `_stamp_local_route_headers()` emission, outcome vocabulary constants, docstrings.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — consumed only: preference constants for the resolved value.
- `proxy/tests/test_routing_preference_logging.py` — `caplog` assertions for the new line (per outcome, once per request, alias normalisation).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — one-line-per-request assertion on the refusal rows (exactly one, not one per branch).

## Dependency graph (wired 2026-10-28)

- Depends on: LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2 (pin), LP-0MVSM06BK008FZUE (deferral), LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4 (too-large promotion) — each stamps the outcome this child reads.
- No dependents: LP-0MVSHXTX1007D58Z / LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57 (tests, docs) consume the implemented behaviour, not this line.
